learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the exciting journey of how a simple idea solves a real-world problem and transforms into a successful business or startup!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An entrepreneur is a person who identifies a problem in society, comes up with an innovative solution, and takes the financial risk to start a business based on that solution.
A startup is a young company founded by entrepreneurs. Unlike traditional businesses (like opening a grocery store), startups usually rely heavily on technology and aim to grow very fast.
Every great startup begins with a problem. For example, 'It's hard to find a taxi in the rain' led to the creation of ride-sharing apps like Uber and Ola.
Before starting, an entrepreneur must plan: Who is the customer? How will the product be made? How will the company make a profit? This blueprint is the business plan.
Starting a company requires capital (money). Entrepreneurs pitch their ideas to 'Investors' who give them money in exchange for a share (equity) in the company.

fun_activity.title: 🚀 The 1-Minute Pitch
fun_activity.instructions: Think of one common problem students face in your school (like heavy bags or cold lunches). Invent a crazy product or app to solve it. Write down a 2-sentence 'pitch' to sell your idea to an investor!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between a regular businessman (runs an established model) and an entrepreneur (introduces innovation and takes higher risks).
📌 Remember that solving a 'Customer Need' is the foundation of any successful startup.
📌 Be ready to explain why startups need investors (they need initial money for research, technology, and marketing before they start making a profit).
quick_recap: ⭐ Failure is a common part of the startup journey; good entrepreneurs learn from their mistakes and try again.
⭐ Startups generate employment and boost the country's overall economy.
⭐ Innovation isn't always a new invention; sometimes it's just finding a faster or cheaper way to do an old task.
